title: Shortly after featuring in the Asian Games, Pokémon UNITE to shut down

blocks.text: Pokémon UNITE will end service in March 2027, just months after featuring in the Asian Games in Nagoya, where the Philippines took home a bronze medal.

The Pokémon Company announced on October 27 that the multiplayer online battle arena game will shut down on March 23, 2027, ending service on both Nintendo Switch and mobile devices. The announcement comes in an unexpected turn for a game that was still part of the regional esports stage at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

The Philippines’ Sibol team secured bronze in Pokémon UNITE after its run ended against Indonesia, adding an Asian Games medal to the country’s esports campaign. The result made the game part of a major international competition shortly before its scheduled closure.

Aeos Gem sales and new UNITE Club memberships have already been suspended, with automatic membership renewals also stopped. Existing members can continue using their benefits until their current membership period ends.

The game will receive a special event and update starting November 12. Players will be able to obtain previously released Unite licenses and Holowear, while a new library feature will let players preserve access to certain records and in-game content after the servers close. Players must download the required library data before the end-of-service date to use the feature afterward.
Competitive play will continue in the meantime. The Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo tournament is still scheduled to take place, with qualifiers beginning December 5, 2026.

For Filipino esports, the announcement puts an unexpected endpoint on a game that recently delivered an international medal. The Philippines’ bronze in Nagoya will remain part of its Asian Games record, even as the game itself heads toward its final months.
